'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Manipur]]
**[[2023 Manipur violence]]
***A video of two women being paraded naked on the streets and subjected to blatant acts of [[Sexual assault|sexual assault]] and [[Gang rape|gang rape]] by a heavily armed mob in [[Manipur]] goes viral, triggering outrage across the country. According to reports, the incident happened on 4 May. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/viral-sexual-assault-video-india-police-action-ethnic-violence-manipur/ (CBS News)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Odesa attacks (2022–present)|Odesa attacks]]
****At least three people are killed and eight [[civilian]]s are injured in a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] strike on [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-warns-ships-black-sea-ukraine-create-temporary-grains-export-route-2023-07-19/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/least-nine-wounded-russian-strike-mykolaiv-governor-2023-07-20/ (Reuters 2)]
****The [[List of diplomatic missions of China|consulate general]] of [[People's Republic of China|China]] in Odesa suffers minor damage during the Russian strike. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/chinese-consular-building-damaged-russian-attack-ukraines-odesa-governor-2023-07-20/ (Reuters)]
***[[2023 Mykolaiv attacks|Mykolaiv attacks]]
****Russian forces strike [[Mykolaiv]], Ukraine, injuring at least 19 civilians. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/least-nine-wounded-russian-strike-mykolaiv-governor-2023-07-20/ (Reuters)] [https://kyivindependent.com/update-18-injured-in-russian-strike-against-mykolaiv-oblast/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')]
**[[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis]]
***The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] reports that it is still awaiting access to the rooftops of Ukraine's [[Russian occupation of Zaporizhzhia Oblast|Russian-occupied]] [[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant]] in [[Enerhodar]], despite being permitted to view the [[Spent fuel pool|fuel cooling pools]] amid allegations of the plant's usage as an [[Nuclear strategy|atomic bargaining chip]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/22/world/americas-emea/iaea-cant-access-nuclear-plant-roof/1901675 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Two policemen are killed and two more injured during a shooting by [[Pakistani Taliban]] gunmen at a checkpoint in [[Peshawar]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/500480-4-terror-attacks-in-48-hours-rock-kp (Geo TV)]
**Two Pakistani Taliban members [[Suicide attack|blow themselves up]] at a police station and government station in [[Bara, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa|Bara]], Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, killing four police officers and wounding eleven more. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/pakistani-taliban-kill-2-policemen-wound-2-gun-101511338 (ABC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021–2023 inflation surge]]
**The [[Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey|Turkish central bank]] raises its main [[interest rate]] from 15% to 17.5% in order to control rising [[inflation]], after the key rate nearly doubled last month. [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/07/20/turkeys-central-bank-raises-interest-rate-less-than-expected-to-17point5percent.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Raigad landslide]]
**Sixteen people are killed and 100 others are believed to be missing during a [[landslide]] in [[Raigad district|Raigad]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/raigad-maharashtra-landslide-live-updates/article67100496.ece (''The Hindu'')]
*Fifty-six people, mostly children, are hospitalized after they suffocated due to inhalation of [[chlorine]] gas that leaked from a swimming pool in [[Alexandria]], [[Egypt]]. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/505149.aspx (''Al-Ahram'')]
*Around 270 people are [[airlift]]ed from a [[Glacier 3000]] [[aerial tramway]] on the [[Tsanfleuron Glacier]] in the [[Diablerets]] [[massif]] in [[Switzerland]] following an electrical failure. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/07/22/world/americas-emea/tourists-evacuated-after-cable-car-malfunction-in-swiss-alps/1901655 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tokelau]]
***[[Tokelau]]'s government announces the first community outbreak of [[COVID-19]] on [[Fakaofo]], the last of country's three atolls to report cases of the virus, as the number of COVID-19 cases exceeds fifty patients. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/493910/entire-village-tested-as-covid-reaches-third-tokelauan-atoll (RNZ)]
*[[2023 European heat waves]]
**At least 110 people are injured during extreme [[hailstorm]]s in [[Veneto]], [[Italy]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/20/extreme-weather-continues-across-europe-as-more-hot-weather-looms (''The Guardian'')]
**A [[state of emergency]] is declared on the island of [[Rhodes]], [[Greece]], with evacuation orders issued for several mountain areas. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/20/extreme-weather-continues-across-europe-as-more-hot-weather-looms (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iraq–Sweden relations]]
**[[Protests against Quran desecration in Sweden]]
***Followers of [[Shia Islam|Shiite]] [[Clergy#Islam|cleric]] [[Muqtada al-Sadr]] set fire to the [[Embassy of Sweden, Baghdad|Swedish embassy]] in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]], in response to a planned [[Quran desecration]] demonstration in [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]]. The [[Ministry for Foreign Affairs (Sweden)|Swedish foreign ministry]] confirms the safety of its embassy staff while the [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Iraq)|Iraqi foreign ministry]] condemns the incident, initiating an investigation to identify those responsible. [https://www.todayonline.com/world/swedish-embassy-baghdad-torched-after-protest-2215201 (AFP via ''Today'')]
***[[Prime Minister of Iraq|Iraqi prime minister]] [[Mohammed Shia' Al Sudani]] directs the foreign ministry to [[Persona non grata|expel]] the Swedish ambassador to Iraq. [https://www.dw.com/en/iraq-expels-swedish-ambassador-over-planned-quran-burning/a-66291449 (DW)]
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction]]
***[[Ministry of Defence (North Korea)|North Korean defence minister]] [[Kang Sun-nam]] warns that the deployment of the [[USS Kentucky (SSBN-737)|USS ''Kentucky'']] [[ballistic missile submarine]] to [[South Korea]] on July 18 could provoke [[North Korea|his country]] to use its [[nuclear weapon]]s under [[Law of North Korea|its law]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/north-korea-submarine-deployment-nuclear-use-fall-under-3642936 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[Bolivia–Iran relations]]
**[[Bolivia]] and [[Iran]] sign a [[memorandum of understanding]] in [[Tehran]], Iran, with both countries vowing to strengthen defence and security cooperation. [https://english.news.cn/20230720/a5ee3e0451b14224b6cbc87080eedaeb/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Russia–European Union relations]]
**The [[European Union]] imposes [[International sanctions|sanctions]] on the director of the [[Federal Penitentiary Service|Russian prison]] incarcerating [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|opposition]] leader [[Alexei Navalny]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/eu-sanctions-chief-of-russian-prison-holding-navalny-dc270f0a (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Auckland shooting]]
**Three people are killed, including the shooter, and six others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[construction]] site in the [[Auckland CBD|central business district]] of [[Auckland]], [[New Zealand]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/part-new-zealands-auckland-cordoned-off-after-reports-shooting-2023-07-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia]]
**[[Prosecutor]]s recommend an additional 20-year prison [[Sentence (law)|sentence]] for Alexei Navalny, who is currently serving a nine-year sentence for [[embezzlement]] and [[contempt of court]], on [[extremism]] charges. [https://guardian.ng/news/russia-seeks-20-years-in-jail-for-kremlin-critic-navalny-allies/ (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup]]
**The ninth edition of the [[FIFA Women's World Cup]] opens in New Zealand, with [[New Zealand women's national football team|the co-hosts]] defeating [[Norway women's national football team|Norway]] 1–0 in the [[2023 FIFA Women's World Cup Group A#New Zealand vs Norway|opening match]] at [[Eden Park]] in Auckland. A [[minute's silence]] was observed prior to the match for the victims of [[2023 Auckland shooting|the shooting that occurred several hours earlier]]. [https://apnews.com/article/womens-world-cup-new-zealand-norway-wilkinson-fed76c62f19d7f04217d96486b03f5f9 (AP)]
